pr_body:
This fixes the case when a `_search` request is targeting multiple aliases that point to the _same data stream_, some being filtered and some unfiltered.

Before this fix, such a scenario would apply the encountered filters as `should` conditions on a `BoolQuery`, despite the request containing an unfiltered (match_all) alias for the same data stream.

This fixes this scenario to disregard the filters when an unfiltered alias is encountered in the resolved expressions, targeting the same data stream.

This also fixes the same scenario for a request that targets the data stream name and a filtered alias (the expected result is that the filter should be disregarded)

Fixes #95786
pr_title: Fix searching a filtered and unfiltered data stream alias

review_comment: This is the bug that we fix in this PR

Why does the predicate not passing for one alias name mean that no aliases are returned? What if `(dsa) -> dsa.getName().contains("foo")` was passed in as the `Predicate<DataStreamAlias> requiredDataStreamAlias` predicate, shouldn't this still go through all of the resolved aliases instead of short-circuiting?

I believe the `required` terminology is a bit confusing here, so I totally understand where you're coming from. 

However, I think the documentation for the method clarifies why `null` is returned
```
Only aliases where the given predicate tests successfully are returned. If the indices list contains a non-required reference to the index itself - null is returned. Returns {@code null} if no filtering is required.
```

I believe the method could use more terminology that references alias filtering as that's what it does. It's currently called in 3 places - in 2 places where we don't care about filtering at all (we just want all the aliases) where the predicates are 
```
aliasMetadata -> true,
dataStreamAlias -> true,
```
and a 3rd place where we are interested in the filtering required where the predicates are 
```
AliasMetadata::filteringRequired, 
DataStreamAlias::filteringRequired
```
This is the bug we fix in this PR
